notes: 'his' before 'house' is the determiner the ASV writes in the article's place (rule 41); no suffix stands in the phrase, and the directive he takes 'into' as its own unit (rule 32).
The attributive participle me'assef follows the noun it modifies and shows none of rule 41's four marks of a predication, so the supplied relative joins the participle rather than being added.
'sat him down' keeps the archaic reflexive with the verb; the competing reading is named in the unit note.
